newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGIP wants Daimler decision on Cap stake.
newsitem.headline: CGIP wants Daimler decision on Cap stake.

text.p: The chairman of French holding company Compagnie Generale d'Industrie et de Participations (CGIP) has urged the other top shareholder in Cap Gemini -- Germany's Daimler-Benz AG -- to decide quickly whether to make an offer for CGIP's 20 percent.

"The Germans have indicated they would like to buy this stake and we have said we may sell it, if that is what they decide," Ernest-Antoine Seilliere told La Tribune business daily in an interview published on Monday.
"We shall see whether they make a concrete proposal. We think it is in everybody's interest that Daimler-Benz makes a rapid decision after all these years of uncertainty," he said.

CGIP, which sold about four percent of the computer systems developer to institutional investors in November, has said it would consider offers from Daimler-Benz or another group for its remaining 20 percent stake if the conditions were right.
Daimler-Benz holds 24.4 percent of Cap Gemini through its Debis subsidiary. Debis said in October it was interested in raising the stake once legislation allowed.
Seilliere said in Monday's interview that whatever came of this, CGIP was pleased with its stake in a company that was set to do well in 1997.
"Whatever happens, our shareholding in Cap Gemini is totally satisfactory for us. This business is recovering rapidly and will make considerable progress in 1997," he said.
He did not give any financial forecasts.
Seilliere indicated recently that a decision on whether to sell the stake would depend on Cap Gemini's strategy plans.

He told a newspaper in December that Cap Gemini had international expansion ambitions but that CGIP did not have the means to be involved in them. However, if the company remained concentrated in Europe, then CGIP could remain a shareholder.
